name: QTT Invitation
description: SaaS lifecycle Phase F. A pending or resolved invite for `email` to join `tenant` with `tenant_role`, optionally also granted `product_role` access to `product` on acceptance. Deliberately a standalone doctype rather than pre-creating a QTT Tenant Membership row with status='invited' (that status option already exists on QTT Tenant Membership, from Phase 1) — `user` is a required field there, and an invitee usually has no Frappe User yet at invite time, so a Membership row simply cannot be created until acceptance. No DocPerm is granted to any tenant-facing role — every read/write goes through qtt_platform.api.invitation.

fields.label: Email
fields.description: The invitee's email — lowercased/validated in validate(). May or may not already have a Frappe User; accept_invitation() handles both.

fields.label: Tenant Role
fields.description: Default is the safe, narrow role — an inviter must deliberately choose Tenant Owner/Admin, never inherit it implicitly.

fields.label: Product
fields.description: Left blank for a tenant-governance-only invite (no product access granted on acceptance).

fields.label: Product Role
fields.description: Required if `product` is set; must be one of that product's own declared role_key values (QTT Product.roles) — validated in validate(), the same rule QTT Product Access itself enforces, never a platform-hardcoded list.

fields.label: Token
fields.description: Opaque, unguessable — generated via frappe.generate_hash(). The accept_invitation() lookup key; never the document name (name is a random hash too, but token is the one deliberately designed to be emailed to an external address).
